results.title: What an NVIDIA H100 costs to rent (Nov 2026): from $1.99/hr
highlights:
# What it costs to rent an NVIDIA H100

NVIDIA H100 prices from every provider listed here, what changes them, and what a month costs.

Prices as of 14 Nov 2026, 14:19 UTC

An NVIDIA H100 rents from $1.99 per GPU-hour on-demand and $1.29 on spot, across the 6 providers listed here. The tables below are this site's current prices: they change when the providers' prices do.

## Every provider's cheapest H100 price

Per GPU per hour, for each version and pricing type. A month is 730 hours of continuous use.

| Provider | Version | Pricing | Per GPU-hour | For 730 hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure | NVL 94 GB | Spot | $1.29 | $942 |
| RunPod | PCIe 80 GB | On-demand | $1.99 | $1,453 |
| Azure | SXM 80 GB | Spot | $2.27 | $1,658 |
| Vultr | 80 GB, version not stated | Spot | $2.30 | $1,679 |
| Nebius | SXM 80 GB | Spot | $2.37 | $1,730 |
| RunPod | NVL 94 GB | On-demand | $2.59 | $1,891 |
| RunPod | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $2.69 | $1,964 |
| Scaleway | PCIe 80 GB | On-demand | $3.17 | $2,313 |
| Scaleway | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $3.50 | $2,555 |
| Scaleway | version not stated | On-demand | $5.30 | $3,868 |
| AWS | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $6.88 | $5,022 |
| Azure | NVL 94 GB | On-demand | $6.98 | $5,095 |
| Azure | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $12.29 | $8,972 |

...

## What changes the price

The version. On-demand, the PCIe 80 GB starts at $1.99, the NVL 94 GB starts at $2.59 and the SXM 80 GB starts at $2.69. PCIe is a card that fits a standard server slot. It runs at lower power than SXM and links to other GPUs more slowly, and it is usually the cheaper version to rent. NVL is a PCIe card made to be paired with a second one over an NVLink bridge, so the two share data quickly. It draws less power than the SXM version. SXM is a module mounted on NVIDIA's HGX board, where GPUs share data over NVLink. It runs at full power with the fastest links between GPUs, which is why 8-GPU training machines use it.

...

Prices are each provider's list price in US dollars per GPU per hour, excluding tax, as of the time shown. Spot capacity can be interrupted and is shown apart from on-demand. Nothing here is a quote or an offer; check the provider before you rent. Euro prices are converted at the European Central Bank rate for 13 Nov 2026.

results.title: 7 best ways to self-host AI inference on cloud GPUs in 2026 (GCP A5X, AWS and Scaleway compared) - Qovery Blog
results.author: Romaric Philogene
highlights:
- Self-hosting inference beats a per-token API only above a utilization break-even. Effective cost per 1M tokens = (GPU $/hour ÷ sustained tokens/hour) x 1,000,000. In the worked example below (gpt-oss-120B on 8x NVIDIA B200), self-hosting beats Together AI's $0.60 per 1M output tokens only above about 33% sustained utilization on Google Cloud DWS Flex-start pricing, and above about 58% on AWS on-demand.
- Renting an A5X-class GPU is the small part of the job. The bigger part is the GPU node pool, NVIDIA drivers and device plugin, an inference server (vLLM, SGLang or NVIDIA Dynamo/Triton), model weight storage and cold starts, GPU-aware autoscaling with scale-to-zero, and someone carrying the pager.
- The three clouds win on different axes. Google Cloud gets the newest NVIDIA silicon first (A5X on Vera Rubin NVL72, GA announced for November 2026). AWS has the deepest discount machinery (Savings Plans up to 72%, Spot up to 90%, Capacity Blocks for ML). Scaleway lists the cheapest H100 hour of the three, at €2.87 in Paris and Warsaw.
- Idle GPUs in dev and staging are the most avoidable line on an inference bill. A GPU node used 40 hours a week but left running all 168 hours spends about 76% of its time producing nothing.
- If you want self-hosted economics without hiring a platform team, run the inference service on Kubernetes inside your own AWS, GCP, Azure or Scaleway account (or your existing cluster) with an internal developer platform such as Qovery. The GPU bill, the committed-use discounts and the prompt data stay in your account.

...

## How does GPU pricing compare across Google Cloud, AWS and Scaleway in 2026?

On published on-demand list prices, Scaleway has the cheapest H100 hour of the three, AWS has the deepest discount machinery, and Google Cloud is where the newest NVIDIA generation lands first. Google Cloud's list prices look expensive, but its committed-use and Flex-start prices change the ranking.

Pricing as of November 6, 2026, normalized to $ (or €) per GPU-hour, US regions for GCP and AWS (their cheapest), Paris and Warsaw for Scaleway:

| Provider | Instance | GPU | On-demand per GPU-hour | Discount mechanisms (max published) | Spot? | Example regions | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g | H100 80GB | $11.06 ($88.49 per 8-GPU VM) | 3-year resource CUD $4.86 (56% off), DWS Flex-start $4.79, Spot up to 91% off | Yes | us-central1 | Committed fleets, H100 on a schedule |
| Google Cloud | a3-ultragpu-8g | H200 141GB | $10.60 ($84.81 per VM) | 3-year CUD $4.65, Flex-start $5.30 | Yes | us-central1 | 70B-class models |
| Google Cloud | a4-highgpu-8g | B200 180GB | No on-demand list price | Flex-start $8.06, 3-year CUD $7.09, Spot $4.95 | Yes | us-central1 | 120B-class models on one node |
| Google Cloud | A5X | Vera Rubin | Not published | Not published | Not published | EMEA expansion announced | Frontier-scale serving |
| AWS | p5.4xlarge / p5.48xlarge | H100 80GB | $6.88 | Savings Plans up to 72%, Spot up to 90%, Capacity Blocks $5.97 | Yes | us-east-1 | Discount stacking, single-GPU H100 |
| AWS | p5en.48xlarge | H200 141GB | $7.91 | Same, Capacity Blocks $7.90 | Yes | us-east-1 | 70B-class models |
| AWS | p6-b200.48xlarge | B200 180GB | $14.24 | Same, Capacity Blocks $14.21 | Yes | us-east-1 | Blackwell without reservations |
| Scaleway | H100-1-80G | H100 PCIe 80GB | €2.87 | Per-minute billing; no Spot market in its public catalog | No | fr-par-2, pl-waw-2 | Cheapest H100 hour in the EU |
| Scaleway | H100-SXM-8-80G | H100 SXM 80GB | €3.17 (€25.33 per 8-GPU instance) | Per-minute billing | No | fr-par-2 | Multi-GPU 70B serving in the EU |
| Scaleway | L40S-1-48G / L4-1-24G | L40S / L4 | €1.47 / €0.79 | Per-minute billing | No | fr-par-2, pl-waw-2 | Small and quantized models |

Sources: Google Cloud accelerator-optimized pricing, Google Cloud Spot VMs, AWS EC2 On-Demand pricing, AWS Savings Plans, AWS Spot, AWS Capacity Blocks pricing, Scaleway GPU pricing (per-minute rates from Scaleway's public product catalog, converted to hourly). The GCP CUD percentage is computed from Google's own 3-year and on-demand prices for a3-highgpu-8g.

What the table tells me:

- Scaleway's €2.87 H100 PCIe hour is less than half of AWS's $6.88 US H100 hour at any recent EUR/USD rate. PCIe H100s are slower than SXM, so compare on measured tokens/s, not on the label. Scaleway's catalog is small and centers on H100, L40S and L4.
- AWS is the cheapest on-demand H100 of the two hyperscalers, and Capacity Blocks for ML let you reserve GPU windows in advance at a dynamic rate charged upfront (AWS).
- Google Cloud's sticker price is the highest, yet its 3-year CUD and Flex-start H100 prices undercut AWS on-demand by about 30%.
- Vera Rubin is Google Cloud-first. AWS has announced Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs for deployment in 2027-2028, with no instance names yet (Amazon).

...

How does GPU pricing compare between Google Cloud, AWS and Scaleway in 2026?

As of November 6, 2026, an H100 costs €2.87/hour on Scaleway (H100 PCIe, Paris and Warsaw), $6.88/hour on AWS on-demand (us-east-1) and $11.06/hour on Google Cloud on-demand (us-central1). Google Cloud's 3-year committed-use price drops its H100 to $4.86/hour, and AWS Savings Plans offer up to 72% off. Google Cloud is the only one of the three announcing Vera Rubin capacity this year.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

The lowest prices often come from marketplaces with variable host quality or from “starting at” prices that are rarely available. The median is a better picture of what a team actually pays for reliable capacity.

...

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
